newsitem.title: JAPAN: Vietnam says to have trade pact with U.S. by Sept.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says to have trade pact with U.S. by Sept.

text.p: Vietnam will reach an agreement with the United States between July and September over their current trade negotiations, central bank governor Cao Sy Kiem said in an interview published on Tuesday.

Kiem, who is attending the 30th annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank in this southern Japanese city, told Japan's Asahi Shimbun newspaper that there were "absolutely no obstacles between the two countries".
He was quoted as saying that as part of its economic reform plan, Vietnam has privatised more than ten of its state-owned enterprises, and hoped to increase this number to 300 companies by next year.

In an earlier speech to the ADB's board of governors, Kiem said Vietnam's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 9.5 percent in 1996, while in the 1991-1995 period the average growth rate had been 8.2 percent.
Exports increased in 1996 by 20 percent and inflation fell to 4.5 percent, he said.

In the first four months of this year, industrial growth reached 13.8 percent year-on-year, and the agricultural growth rate was expected to be four to five percent thanks to a bumper crop, Kiem said. Meanwhile, the consumer price index rose by 1.5 percent, its lowest-ever rate, he said.
In the same period, exports increased by 33.8 percent while imports were up 7.7 percent year-on-year, he added.
Kiem said foreign direct investment in Vietnam was rising by 30 percent annually, and the total stood at $30 billion.
Vietnam is the ADB's fifth-largest borrower at $333 million. Kiem said Hanoi had received cumulative official development assistance of $8 billion since it began its economic reforms.
